title: Carrot & turmeric bar soap
subtitle: A golden bar with a gentle warming tint
excerpt: Cold-process bar soap made with carrot juice in place of water, coloured and lightly scented by ground turmeric. The beta-carotene from the carrot gives the finished bar a warm, honey-gold colour. Made on an olive, coconut, and castor base; yields eight bars; hardens in 4-6 weeks.
sourceNotes: Susan Miller Cavitch, The Soapmaker's Companion (1997), liquid substitution guidance for cold-process soap (replacing water with juices or milks). Soap-Calc SAP values (accessed 2026): coconut oil 0.190, olive oil 0.134, castor oil 0.128. Turmeric as a natural soap colourant: trace amounts used; does not stain skin at 0.5% inclusion. Carrot juice in soap: the sugars can accelerate trace and heat the gel phase.

recipe.batchNotes: The sugar in carrot juice makes the lye reaction run hot. Freeze the carrot juice to slush before adding the lye to slow the reaction and protect the beta-carotene. Don't double the batch without re-checking temperatures.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The golden colour deepens over the cure. Bars are at their best at 6 weeks and keep well for 18 months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 18 months in a cool, dry cupboard. The beta-carotene and turmeric pigments fade over time but the bar stays effective. Discard if the bar develops DOS (orange spots) or smells rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: The point at which a cold-process soap batter thickens enough to hold a faint trail drizzled on its surface, the signal to pour into the mould.

The chemical reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide (lye) that produces soap and glycerol. Carrot juice is used in place of water; the lye still dissolves into liquid and the reaction proceeds identically.
The percentage of oil left unsaponified in the finished bar, contributing a conditioning quality. This recipe uses a 5% superfat.

content.text: Carrot and turmeric soap is a golden-coloured cold-process bar made with fresh carrot juice replacing the water, and a small amount of ground turmeric stirred through at trace. The beta-carotene from the carrot juice tints the finished bar honey-gold. Made on olive, coconut, and castor oils, it lathers well and washes off clean. Eight bars; hardens in 4-6 weeks.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: 50% of oil weight; pure (not extra virgin); conditioning base
40% of oil weight; melt gently; hardness and lather
NaOH at 99% purity; calculated for 5% superfat; always add lye to liquid
fresh; freeze to a slush before use to control heat spike; provides beta-carotene colour
0.5% of oil weight; stirred in at trace; adds warm golden colour

content.text: Method
Prepare the carrot lye solution

Put on protective gloves and goggles. Pour the carrot juice into ice-cube trays and freeze to slush (about 2 hours). The frozen slush slows the exothermic reaction and prevents the sugars from scorching and turning brown.

Place the carrot juice slush into the HDPE pitcher. Add the sodium hydroxide slowly, a little at a time, stirring as you go. Do not pour the lye all at once into frozen liquid as chunks can form around a pocket of unreacted lye. Stir until fully dissolved. The solution will turn orange from the beta-carotene.
Cool the lye solution to 38-42°C.
Prepare the oils and blend to trace
Melt the coconut oil, combine with olive and castor oils, and bring to 38-42°C.
Pour the lye solution into the oils. Stick-blend in short bursts until
trace
. Stir in the ground turmeric by hand.

Pour into the silicone mould. Insulate with a towel and leave 24-48 hours. The batter may run very hot during gel phase because of the carrot juice sugars. Leave the mould uncovered if it feels hot to the touch.
Unmould, cut, and cure
Unmould when firm. Cut into 8 bars wearing gloves. Cure on a rack for 4-6 weeks.
The
saponification
is complete when a corner touched to the tongue gives no zap. The golden colour deepens during cure.
Storage and shelf life
Keep cured bars on a ventilated rack in a cool, dry place. The
superfat

keeps the bar conditioning; the golden colour fades over 12-18 months but the bar itself stays good. Use within 18 months. Discard if the cut face develops orange spots (DOS) or the bar smells sharp rather than faintly earthy.
